title: Knowledge-Guided Construction of Machine Learning Potentials for Reactive Behavior in Energetic Materials
title_zh: 文献研究：Knowledge-Guided Construction of Machine Learning Potentials for Reactive Behavior in Energetic Materials
summary: Energetic materials involve multiple interactions, making reliable machine-learning potentials (MLPs) difficult to construct without extensive datasets. Here, we enhance the ability of the neural netw…
abstract: arXiv:2610.17987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Energetic materials involve multiple interactions, making reliable machine-learning potentials (MLPs) difficult to construct without extensive datasets. Here, we enhance the ability of the neural network interatomic potential (NNAP) to describe molecular systems using sphmulti, a refined spherical-harmonic basis set that combines extra radial basis with element-specific chemical weighting in each radial channel. We further integrate hyperactive learning, farthest-point sampling, and iterative sufficiency criteria with knowledge-guided key events, enabling the NNAP to retain essential information for describing the material system. For 3,3'-diamino-4,4'-azoxyfurazan, the resulting NNAP is trained on only 13,680 configurations yet captures key properties, including the isomerization barrier, pyrolysis activation energy, and shock Hugoniot behavior. NNAP-driven molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that pyrolysis proceeds through furazan-ring opening followed by chain reactions, whereas shock loading induces anisotropic hydrogen transfer driven by interlayer structural deformations. This work enables efficient and reliable MLPs for energetic materials.

title: Benchmarking machine-learning interatomic potentials using classical force fields
title_zh: 使用经典力场对机器学习原子间势进行基准测试
summary: 我们通过测试几种著名的机器学习原子间势（线性原子团簇扩展、Behler-Parrinello 高维神经网络势和基于图神经网络的 MACE 势）对它们拟合经典势（如 Lennard-Jones 和 Stillinger-Weber 势）的性能进行理性比较。由此，我们评估了它们在几个方面的优点和局限性：不同的训练数据集大小、对噪声的鲁棒性、碳足迹，以及重现径向分布函数作为可观察示例的能力。
abstract: arXiv:2610.14239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a rational comparison between several well-known machine-learning interatomic potentials (linear atomic cluster expansion, the Behler-Parrinello high-dimensional neural network potential, and the graph neural network-based MACE potential) by testing their performance for fitting classical potentials such as the Lennard-Jones and Stillinger-Weber potential. With this we assess their advantages and limitations regarding several aspects: varying training dataset size, robustness to noise, carbon footprint, as well as the ability to reproduce the radial distribution function as an example observable. Overall the MACE models are shown to most accurately reproduce the potential energy surface, with little sign of overfitting, but at a significant computational cost, highlighting important questions regarding the choice of models in computational materials science.

title: Indirect prediction and screening of frustrated magnetic materials using machine learning
title_zh: 使用机器学习间接预测和筛选受阻磁性材料
summary: 磁挫败通常通过挫败指数来量化，挫败指数是根据居里-维斯和尼尔温度计算得出的。由于大多数材料无法同时获得这两个量，因此直接预测磁挫败指数仍然具有挑战性。在这里，我们提出了一种机器学习工作流程，用于间接预测挫败指数，并通过独立预测居里-维斯和尼尔温度来筛选潜在的挫败磁性化合物。在我们的工作中，通过 CatBoost 算法实现的基于成分的模型，在实验数据上进行训练，并使用化学信息数据集细分进行优化。稀土氧化物模型在尼尔预测中和稀土模型在居里-魏斯预测中获得了最高的预测精度。
abstract: arXiv:2610.15683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic frustration is commonly quantified by the frustration index, calculated from the Curie-Weiss and Neel temperatures. Because both quantities are not simultaneously available for most materials, direct prediction of the magnetic frustration index remains challenging. Here, we propose a machine learning workflow for indirect prediction of the frustration index and consequent screening of potential frustrated magnetic compounds through independent prediction of Curie-Weiss and Neel temperatures. In our work, composition-based models implemented via the CatBoost algorithm, trained on experimental data were optimized using chemically informed dataset subdivision. The highest predictive accuracy was achieved for the rare earth-oxide model in predicting Neel and for the rare earth model in predicting Curie-Weiss. Ensemble uncertainty was incorporated through a conservative frustration index to improve the reliability of candidate selection. Screening of approximately 67000 Materials Project compounds identified 20 high-confidence frustrated magnetic candidates, including several experimentally known frustrated magnets and previously unexplored oxide systems potential for further investigation.

title: Modelling the dynamics of the martensitic transformation in Ni₂MnGa with machine-learning force-fields
title_zh: 利用机器学习力场对 Ni2MnGa 中马氏体相变的动力学进行建模
summary: 化学计量 Ni2MnGa 和相关 Heusler 合金中的马氏体转变受到电子结构、磁性和晶格动力学之间微妙的相互作用的控制。虽然密度泛函理论（DFT）已经成功地绘制了调制马氏体的能量图，但它在计算上仍然无法捕获相关长度和时间尺度的有限温度动态。在这里，我们通过构建从头开始分子动力学插值的 DFT 训练的机器学习力场 (ML-FF) 来弥补这一差距。
abstract: arXiv:2610.16467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The martensitic transformations in stoichiometric Ni₂MnGa and related Heusler alloys are governed by a delicate interplay between electronic structure, magnetism, and lattice dynamics. While density functional theory (DFT) has successfully mapped the energy landscape of modulated martensites, it remains computationally prohibitive for capturing finite-temperature dynamics across relevant length and time scales. Here, we bridge this gap by constructing DFT-trained machine-learning force-fields (ML-FF) interpolated from ab initio molecular dynamics. We demonstrate that ML-FF trained on DFT data can reproduce key features of Ni₂MnGa, including the soft TA₂ phonon and a preference for nanotwinned martensites. Using classical molecular dynamics simulations, we explore the impact of adaptive nanotwinning on the austenite-martensite transition, which facilitates the dynamics of both, forward and backward transformation. We demonstrate, that the negative twin boundary energy along the entire transformations path predicted by DFT for T=0, supports the formation of ordered modulated martensites at finite temperatures. Our results pave the way for large-scale simulations of magnetic shape memory alloys with near-DFT accuracy.

summary: Aggregation of ion pairs formed during CO 2 capture may govern absorption thermodynamics and kinetics, but it is often overestimated by fixed-charge classical force fields. Here, we demonstrate the pr…
abstract: Aggregation of ion pairs formed during CO 2 capture may govern absorption thermodynamics and kinetics, but it is often overestimated by fixed-charge classical force fields. Here, we demonstrate the promise of graph neural network interatomic potentials, which offer quantum-level accuracy, for directly evaluating the aggregation tendencies of ionic products in CO 2 -loaded aqueous amine solutions.
journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

title: Large Out-of-plane Polarization in Two-dimensional Bi2O3 Monolayers Predicted by an AI-driven Inverse-design Workflow
title_zh: AI 驱动的逆向设计工作流程预测二维 Bi2O3 单层膜中的大面外偏振
summary: 具有内置电场的二维（2D）极性氧化物为纳米级电子学、光电子学和表面电荷工程提供了有前景的机会。然而，由于非层状氧化物网络结构的巨大复杂性，他们的发现仍然具有挑战性。在这里，我们将逆向结构设计与机器学习原子间势和第一原理计算相结合，以探索二维氧化物构型。使用 Bi2O3 作为代表性系统，我们识别出两种先前未报道的具有四方和斜方对称性的极性单层。两种结构都表现出垂直分离的 Bi 和 O 子层，产生明显的固有极性，贝里相 2D 极化分别为 34.12 和 37.15 pC/m。
abstract: arXiv:2610.14429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) polar oxides with built-in electric fields offer promising opportunities for nanoscale electronics, optoelectronics, and surface charge engineering. However, their discovery remains challenging due to the enormous structural complexity of nonlayered oxide networks. Here, we combine inverse structural design with a machine-learning interatomic potential and first-principles calculations to explore 2D oxide configurations. Using Bi2O3 as a representative system, we identify two previously unreported polar monolayers with tetragonal and orthorhombic symmetries. Both structures exhibit vertically separated Bi and O sublayers, giving rise to pronounced intrinsic polarity with Berry-phase 2D polarizations of 34.12 and 37.15 pC/m, respectively. Notably, the o-Bi2O3 monolayer exhibits one of the largest reported out-of-plane polarizations among 2D oxides. Both monolayers exhibit dynamical stability, finite-temperature structural integrity, and wide band gaps (~3.8 eV). The large polarization originates from dimensionality-induced reconstruction of the nonlayered Bi-O network, which breaks local coordination symmetry and produces out-of-plane charge redistribution, while the stereochemically active Bi 6s2 lone pair further favors asymmetric Bi-O bonding. These findings suggest dimensionality-induced local-coordination symmetry breaking as a promising design motif for high-polarization 2D oxides, and demonstrate the utility of combining inverse design with machine-learning-assisted screening to explore unconventional polar phases in nonlayered oxide networks.

title: Can Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials Capture Small Polarons? A Geometry-Based Benchmark in Transition-Metal Oxides
title_zh: 文献研究：Can Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials Capture Small Polarons? A Geometry-Based Benchmark in Transition-Metal Oxides
summary: Small polarons, formed when excess electrons become localized through lattice distortions, play a critical role in charge transport, catalysis, and degradation processes in transition-metal (TM) oxide…
abstract: arXiv:2610.17352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small polarons, formed when excess electrons become localized through lattice distortions, play a critical role in charge transport, catalysis, and degradation processes in transition-metal (TM) oxides. Whether universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs), which lack explicit electronic degrees of freedom, can describe them remains unclear. Here, we investigate H-induced electron localization across a range of TM oxides using a geometric descriptor based on TM-O bond-length expansion (Z-score) to identify polaronic distortions. We find that uMLIPs exhibit varying degrees of electron localization, from delocalized states to metastable small polarons, with their behavior strongly dependent on the training data and treatment of electronic correlations. In particular, the absence of Hubbard U corrections for specific TM cations in the training data leads to electron delocalization, in contrast to DFT+U predictions. Although some uMLIPs reproduce polaron hopping barriers during coupled proton-polaron transfer, all of them fail to stabilize spatially separated polaron-donor configurations, instead favoring localization near the H dopant.

title: Toward a Multimodal Foundation Model for Plasma State Reconstruction
title_zh: 文献研究：Toward a Multimodal Foundation Model for Plasma State Reconstruction
summary: Plasma experiments observe coupled physical states through sparse, heterogeneous, and incomplete diagnostics. We present a proof of concept toward a multimodal foundation model for plasma state recons…
abstract: arXiv:2610.15076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Plasma experiments observe coupled physical states through sparse, heterogeneous, and incomplete diagnostics. We present a proof of concept toward a multimodal foundation model for plasma state reconstruction during magnetic reconnection, motivated by the Facility for Laboratory Reconnection Experiments (FLARE). Using 250 synthetic VPIC simulations at fixed reference electron beta βₑ₀=0.2, with 225 training runs and 25 disjoint validation runs, we train a 5.5M-parameter residual 3D U-Net to reconstruct three magnetic-field components and electron density from incomplete observations. The model combines spatial-only pooling, which preserves all 24 temporal frames, with global spatiotemporal self-attention and rotary positional encoding. Independently masking magnetic and density modalities across random, grid, block, and temporal patterns enables sparse sensing, cross-modal completion, density super-resolution, and temporal completion with a single set of weights and no task-specific retraining. With density fully hidden, just 0.1% magnetic spatial visibility reduces median density NRMSE from approximately 0.9 to 0.1. Conversely, observed density improves current-density reconstruction when magnetic data are absent or extremely sparse. With no magnetic observations, roughly 1% density visibility approaches the density reconstruction accuracy achieved with fully observed magnetic fields, although current structure remains more dependent on direct magnetic measurements. Full magnetic conditioning also stabilizes completion of missing future density frames. These results demonstrate bidirectional cross-modal predictive coupling within this simulation regime. Generalization across plasma regimes or to experimental measurements remains untested.

title: Solvating machine-learning interatomic potentials for solution-phase chemistry
title_zh: 文献研究：Solvating machine-learning interatomic potentials for solution-phase chemistry
summary: Most machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are trained on gas-phase data, which limits their use for chemistry in solution. Here, we introduce AnySolv, a transferable implicit solvation pote…
abstract: arXiv:2610.17226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are trained on gas-phase data, which limits their use for chemistry in solution. Here, we introduce AnySolv, a transferable implicit solvation potential that provides solvent-dependent energy and force corrections to existing gas-phase potentials without retraining them. It is trained on 1.4 million solvation energies and forces computed with density functional theory (DFT) and SMD in 36 solvents, spanning charged, open-shell, and transition-state structures. Because solvents are represented by continuous physical descriptors, AnySolv supports 179 solvents, including those absent from training. On external benchmarks, AnySolv reproduces DFT-SMD solvation energies to 2-4 meV mean absolute error at more than three orders of magnitude lower cost, and it matches the accuracy of DFT-SMD against experimental solvation free energies. This enables screening of the mechanisms of 120 nucleophilic aromatic substitution reactions in six phases as well as molecular dynamics simulations that reproduce the experimentally observed solvent-dependent conformational preferences of alanine dipeptide. By providing transferable solvation corrections to existing MLIPs, AnySolv enables scalable simulations of solvent-dependent chemical reactivity and molecular dynamics.

title: Accurately Generalizing Deep-Learning Hamiltonian Methods to Plane-Wave Density Functional Theory
title_zh: 文献研究：Accurately Generalizing Deep-Learning Hamiltonian Methods to Plane-Wave Density Functional Theory
summary: Deep neural networks that predict density functional theory (DFT) Hamiltonians from material structures offer a route to efficient electronic-structure calculations. However, extending localized atomi…
abstract: arXiv:2610.18317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep neural networks that predict density functional theory (DFT) Hamiltonians from material structures offer a route to efficient electronic-structure calculations. However, extending localized atomic-orbital (AO) Hamiltonian learning to plane-wave (PW) calculations with hybrid functionals requires a compact AO representation that preserves the effects of nonlocal operators. Here we propose a projectability-guided construction of nonorthogonal AO Hamiltonians from a small, selected set of PW eigenstates and eigenvalues. High-projectability states are retained, and selected higher-energy states complete the AO subspace, avoiding an empirical shift and its arbitrary contribution to the learning targets. Because the construction uses PW eigenstates and eigenvalues, it incorporates nonlocal contributions present in the reference calculation without explicitly reconstructing their AO matrix elements. Benchmarks for MoS2 and sodium phases show accurate reproduction of PW bands with smaller AO bases than real-space reconstruction. The resulting PBE and HSE Hamiltonians can be learned by equivariant neural networks, connecting PW reference calculations with electronic-structure prediction. This approach broadens the range of PW DFT calculations available for AO Hamiltonian learning and enables compact, accurate training targets for developing more widely applicable electronic-structure models.

title: Material and thermal properties of MgCl 2 molten salt by ab initio and machine-learning molecular-dynamics simulations
title_zh: 文献研究：Material and thermal properties of MgCl 2 molten salt by ab initio and machine-learning molecular-dynamics simulations
summary: We study the structural, thermophysical, and dynamical properties of molten MgCl 2 over a wide temperature range using Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics (AIMD) and molecular dynamics simulations based on m…
abstract: We study the structural, thermophysical, and dynamical properties of molten MgCl 2 over a wide temperature range using Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics (AIMD) and molecular dynamics simulations based on machine-learning interaction potentials (MLIPs). MLIPs can achieve near-AIMD accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost, enabling simulations of larger systems and longer timescales. This opens up the possibility of studying the system under out-of-equilibrium conditions, which in turn allows for the calculation of physical properties, such as the thermal conductivity or viscosity, that cannot be obtained reliably for the typical time and length scales accessible to AIMD. We follow two complementary approaches to develop and evaluate the MLIPs. First, we develop a Deep Potential (DP) from scratch using AIMD trajectories at different temperatures. Second, we also evaluate two out-of-the-box foundation models and a fine-tuned version of one of them. The fine-tuning is performed using configurations from the AIMD trajectories originally used to train the DP. We compare the predictions of the trained DP, the foundation models, and AIMD simulations with the available experimental data and provide a comprehensive calculation of the most important physical quantities of molten MgCl 2 . We compute densities, radial and angular distribution functions, thermal conductivity, heat capacity, viscosity, and diffusion coefficients over the 1000–1600 K temperature range. This range is relevant to important technological applications such as thermal energy storage, generation IV nuclear reactors, and concentrated solar power systems. Finally, we briefly review the accuracy and performance of the different MLIP versions used throughout the work.
journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

title: Extrapolating Collisional Rate Coefficients for Molecules of Astrophysical Interest Using Neural Networks
title_zh: 文献研究：Extrapolating Collisional Rate Coefficients for Molecules of Astrophysical Interest Using Neural Networks
summary: State-to-state rate coefficients for inelastic molecular collisions are essential inputs for non-local thermodynamic equilibrium radiative transfer models, yet their computation using quantum scatteri…
abstract: arXiv:2610.18278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: State-to-state rate coefficients for inelastic molecular collisions are essential inputs for non-local thermodynamic equilibrium radiative transfer models, yet their computation using quantum scattering methods is prohibitive for large molecules and highly excited rotational states. We investigate the ability of artificial neural networks to extend existing datasets of collisional excitation rate coefficients without performing additional scattering calculations. A multilayer perceptron model was trained using molecular quantum numbers, level energies, energy gaps, and kinetic temperature as descriptors, and optimized on logarithmic rate coefficients. The model was tested on diverse collision systems ranging from simple diatomic molecules (CO, SiO) to open-shell species (SO), small asymmetric tops (H₂O, SO₂), and complex organic molecules (benzonitrile and vinyl cyanide) colliding with H₂ molecules or He atoms. Extrapolations were performed toward higher rotational levels, higher temperatures, and combinations of both. For most systems, predictions of rate coefficients involving previously unseen rotational states yielded mean error factors between 1.1 and 1.5, with the dominant rate coefficients generally reproduced more accurately than weaker transitions. Temperature extrapolations proved particularly successful, while combined extrapolations in temperature and rotational levels remained accurate to within a factor of two in most cases. The prediction quality depends on the interplay between dataset size, temperature range, molecular complexity, and the presence of clear collisional propensity rules. Overall, the approach demonstrates that machine learning can provide a practical route to extending collisional datasets for astrophysical applications, especially for large molecules for which additional quantum-scattering calculations are computationally demanding.

title: Transfer learning-aided, artificial intelligence approach to evaluate optical properties of materials for classical and quantum photonic applications
title_zh: 文献研究：Transfer learning-aided, artificial intelligence approach to evaluate optical properties of materials for classical and quantum photonic applications
summary: In this study, an artificial intelligence-assisted evaluation of the refractive indices of different materials is performed. The evaluation of the refractive index is necessary to design photonic devi…
abstract: arXiv:2610.15904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, an artificial intelligence-assisted evaluation of the refractive indices of different materials is performed. The evaluation of the refractive index is necessary to design photonic devices for various classical and quantum photonic applications, and to theoretically analyse experimental results. The refractive index is one of the crucial parameters that affect the interaction of light with matter. Although the refractive index can be measured experimentally, its estimation via computational means provide the advantage of not requiring costly instrumentation, trained researchers and could avoid potential laboratory-based uncertainties. Therefore, in this study, artificial intelligence is implemented to estimate the optical constants of two types of materials, i.e., noble metals, and semiconductors. To this end, an artificial neural network is used to estimate the real and the imaginary parts of the refractive index of a specific material for various wavelengths of light. Then, the knowledge of the trained neural network is employed to initiate and train new neural networks to estimate the refractive indices of other materials. For the training of a neural network, various methods can be deployed. However, the application of the training can be a time-consuming process. A transfer learning approach is here implemented to provide a faster training solution for the problem under study. The implementation of transfer learning allows training the neural networks for a new material with higher speed or accuracy when compared to non-knowledge transfer-based training. Our results show the efficiency of the proposed technique in accurately evaluating the real and imaginary parts of the refractive index of different materials.

title: Two-atom interaction potential database supporting physics-informed features for machine learning and material property prediction
title_zh: 文献研究：Two-atom interaction potential database supporting physics-informed features for machine learning and material property prediction
summary: Accurately predicting the energy and relevant properties of molecules and complex crystalline systems remains a cornerstone of computational materials science. While density functional theory (DFT) of…
abstract: Accurately predicting the energy and relevant properties of molecules and complex crystalline systems remains a cornerstone of computational materials science. While density functional theory (DFT) offers high accuracy, its computational cost scales prohibitively for large-scale materials. In this work, we present a comprehensive, first-principles-derived database of two-atom interaction potentials and interatomic forces to accelerate the property prediction via physics-informed machine learning. Computed using spin-polarized DFT via the GPAW package, the database encompasses all 2346 possible atomic pairs generated from 68 unique elements as a function of interatomic distance. The practical utility of this database was demonstrated within the many-body expansion framework by engineering highly descriptive features to predict three distinct types of energy for benchmarking. First, the framework was applied to predict the total energy of molecules within the G2/97 database. Second, for defect energetics on 2D materials (the IMP2D database), localized concentric shell potentials and spatial gradients were introduced to capture the formation energy of adsorbate defects. Finally, for molecular energetics within the QM9 database, we developed advanced descriptors, including a potential-based matrix, a two-body Bag of Bonds, and a three-body Ray’s asymmetric parameter histogram to evaluate atomization energy. Evaluated using kernel ridge regression, the combined two-body and three-body feature set yielded an outstanding test result with the mean absolute error of 0.186 eV ( R 2 = 0.9994) on a 10 000-samples subset. This framework showcases the power of utilizing explicit, database-derived potentials as robust descriptors for high-fidelity predictions of energy and relevant properties.
journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

title: PolyFKAN: Integrating Fourier-KAN layers into graph neural networks for polymer property prediction
title_zh: 文献研究：PolyFKAN: Integrating Fourier-KAN layers into graph neural networks for polymer property prediction
summary: Graph neural networks have become a central tool for polymer property prediction, but their fixed activation functions can impose a low-pass spectral bias that smooths over the sharp, multi-scale stru…
abstract: Graph neural networks have become a central tool for polymer property prediction, but their fixed activation functions can impose a low-pass spectral bias that smooths over the sharp, multi-scale structure–property variations that distinguish chemically similar polymers. We address this limitation with PolyFKAN, a multitask graph-learning architecture that augments the prediction head of a polyGNN backbone with Fourier Kolmogorov–Arnold network layers. PolyFKAN represents edge-wise activations as truncated Fourier series and couples the resulting spectral branch to the standard multilayer perceptron (MLP) pathway through a bounded residual gate, thereby increasing functional expressivity without disrupting the learned graph embeddings. Across 17 polymer properties spanning electronic, thermodynamic, optical/dielectric, thermal, and gas-permeability domains, PolyFKAN achieves statistically significant improvement over a tightly controlled polyGNN baseline on 11 of 17 targets (one-sided t -test, p < 0.05), with one additional target showing marginal improvement. The gains are especially pronounced for multi-scale properties, including more than 15% average root mean squared error reduction for large-penetrant gas permeabilities and more than 15% improvement across optical and dielectric targets. Hierarchical ablation further reveals that optimal Fourier bandwidth is property-dependent: difficult, multi-scale targets require broader spectral capacity with stronger amplitude control, whereas high-fidelity targets benefit from lighter regularization. These results establish Fourier-KAN prediction heads as a minimally invasive and physically aligned inductive bias for polymer informatics.
journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

title: Wisevolve Potential Engine: Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics at 100 Million Atom-Steps per Second on a Single GPU
title_zh: 文献研究：Wisevolve Potential Engine: Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics at 100 Million Atom-Steps per Second on a Single GPU
summary: General-purpose molecular dynamics software supports diverse interatomic potentials and simulation requirements. Within a simulation stage, the loaded potential model and the required calculations typ…
abstract: arXiv:2610.17366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: General-purpose molecular dynamics software supports diverse interatomic potentials and simulation requirements. Within a simulation stage, the loaded potential model and the required calculations typically remain fixed as the atomic configuration evolves. We present the Wisevolve Potential Engine (WPE), which uses this information from GPUMD to select and reuse a GPU execution policy tailored to the model and simulation stage. GPUMD retains simulation control and ownership of the simulation data. On a single NVIDIA RTX 5090, WPE-enabled GPUMD (GPUMD-WPE) achieves a median throughput of 109 million atom-step/s across 106 neuroevolution potential (NEP) workloads. For a 15.1-million-atom diamond Si system, it sustains 142 million atom-step/s. Relative to GPUMD, geometric-mean speedups are 3.49x across these NEP workloads, 3.61x across 16 workloads using NEP with dynamic charges (qNEP), 1.24x across 28 classical-potential workloads, and 10.5x across 56 path-integral molecular dynamics (PIMD) configurations. End-to-end calculations of water structure, lattice thermal conductivity, and PIMD thermal expansion show close agreement with corresponding GPUMD results and published simulation results. A separate 12.5-million-atom Cu shock-compression simulation demonstrates its applicability to large-scale nonequilibrium dynamics. These results support model- and stage-specific specialization as a practical way to accelerate GPU potential evaluation in general-purpose molecular dynamics workflows.

title: Fourier-Space Approach to Physics-Informed Magnetization Reconstruction from Nitrogen-Vacancy Measurements
title_zh: 文献研究：Fourier-Space Approach to Physics-Informed Magnetization Reconstruction from Nitrogen-Vacancy Measurements
summary: Author(s): Alexander Setescak, Florian Bruckner, Dieter Suess, Young-Gwan Choi, Hayden Binger, Lotte Boer, Chenhui Zhang, Hyunsoo Yang, Claire Donnelly, Uri Vool, and Claas Abert Reconstructing magnet…
